items: A calmer, simpler layout: one account menu, Classic settings tucked under Customize, fewer cards on Play, folded Stats sections and compact OA tiles.
Sign in with Google everywhere, including the Windows app, which finishes in your browser. Passwords are retired: if you used one before, sign in once and link Google.
Fits any window size: snap Zetapro to half, a third or a quarter of the screen and every page and game keeps its main button in view.
A cleaner window on Windows: the top bar replaces the old white title bar and matches light and dark themes, with slimmer scrollbars.
Much faster with a long history: Play, Drill and Stats redraw almost instantly, the first visit to Stats is about three times quicker, and the app opens faster, most of all on phones.
Sturdier saving and sync: desktop saves survive power cuts and locked files, phone saves no longer get stuck, syncs do less repeat work, and phone updates arrive reliably.
Better OA questions: in NumberLogic the right answer can be any of the five options, and Beat the Odds no longer offers impossible or 0%/100% options.
Trouble problems stay until you review them, and "slow" means slow for you at the time.

Fixes: Enter during the 3-2-1, in a Goal box (an empty box now keeps your goal) and in the sign-in dialog; a hardware keyboard with the on-screen pad; held keys or double-clicks answering twice; holding Space in Balloon; and quitting at Quick play game over, which now counts.
Leaderboard: joining, renaming and leaving are much faster. Screen readers hear answer feedback in the OA games, and quick taps no longer zoom on phones.

Quick play: a casual way to practise every OA module. You get three lives, combos for answers in a row, a speed bonus, and a clock that gets faster as you level up. Your best shows on the OA page. Test mode is unchanged.
The Zap-N games have a little more life: floating points, a streak counter in Code Compare, and optional sound effects (off until you turn them on).

Skill levels: Stats shows a level for each operation and problem type from your recent speed (level 6 is fast enough for a Classic score of 60–69). Results tell you when one goes up, and Stats lists the types closest to their next level.
Weekly goal: pick how many days a week you want to practise (3 by default, or Off). A new Practice card on the Play page shows this week against it, with a short recap of last week.
Trouble problems come back on a schedule: the day after a slip, then 3 and 7 days later, and retire after three clean reviews on separate days. The Drill page shows how many are due today.
Next up: the Play page suggests one thing to practise, with the reason.
Leaderboards open on Classic, and Classic and 80 in 8 scores now post as soon as the round ends.
Leaderboards: see where you rank on the Daily Challenge, Classic, 80 in 8 and every OA module, this week and all time. Anyone can view them.
Join once with a nickname and it follows your account to every device. Your best scores post after each round, and your email is never shown. Leaving removes your scores.
Intervals: a range that holds the answer but starts at 0 now says "Contained" and explains why it scores 0, instead of "Missed".
Intervals: "greater than" questions no longer ask for counts close to zero, which no sensible range could score.

Full OA practice: take every module in Optiver's order, with breaks between stages as long as you like. A closing report rates each module and lists your biggest point losses, each with what to practise.

Every OA module is recalibrated to the real test's difficulty, leaning hard: "pick the closest" answers in Beat the Odds, a harder NumberLogic tier, chart and graph questions in Likelihood-list, big grids, coin tables and trends in Intervals (45 s each), 6–8 card Orderbooks boards, and tougher Zap-N games.
Stats → OA: hover a module's trend to see each recent test as a point, with its date, score and time taken.
Stats has a Classic / OA switch. OA shows every module's scores and trend, your weakest topics across all rounds, and lets you reopen any past round's review.
The OA tab now sits right after Play.

New OA tab: practice for every part of Optiver's online assessment. Beat the Odds, NumberLogic, Likelihood-list, Intervals, Orderbooks and the Zap-N games, each with a timed Test mode and a Learn mode that explains every answer.
Daily Challenge: one shared 120-second set a day. Your first try counts, and Copy result shares your score without spoilers.
A practice calendar and streak on the Play page.
Press Tab to restart a round instantly. Results now show how far you were from your best.
On phones, Start is on the first screen of the Play page.
"Classic" is now the one name for the Zetamac-style mode. Manage data puts backups first and bulk deletes last.
Safer sync: a device that loses its saved games now downloads them again instead of removing them from your account.
Signing out can also clear this device, for shared phones and computers. Your games stay in your account.
Typing in the account dialog is no longer interrupted when a sync finishes.
Sign in with Google or email to sync your games across devices: no GitHub tokens needed.
Syncing is now instant and only sends what changed.
Export and import a backup file of all your games (Manage data).
The Windows app signs in with email and password; add a password to a Google account in the browser version.
On-screen number pad on phones: no more keyboard popping up over the problem.
Optional 3-2-1 countdown before a round, and the timer turns red for the last 10 seconds.
Undo after deleting games, and restore games from any earlier synced version.
Results show how you did against your recent average and your goal.
Clearer wording: "Slowdown" instead of "Cost".
Tabs sit at the bottom of the screen on phones.
The Windows app tells you when a new version is out.
Zetamac-style game with per-type stats, factor map, mistake patterns and trouble problems.
Smart, trouble and custom drills, with smart drill stats and pace tracking.
Optiver-style 80 in 8 with net scoring and per-type stats.
Goals, sync across devices through a private GitHub repo, and a phone app.
